overview: Black answers the King's Gambit with an early check on h4, trying to disrupt White's king before developing. White usually blocks with 3.g3 and gets a lead in development and open play while the black queen has to run. I am unsure of the exact theory, but it is regarded as a risky early queen sortie that stronger players avoid.

white_ideas.idea: Block with g3 to gain a tempo on the queen, then develop quickly with Nf3 and Nc3.
Use the open f- and e-files and a lead in development to punish the early queen.

black_ideas.idea: Grab e4 with the queen or keep ...exf4 pressure to exploit the weakened kingside.
Develop with tempo against the queen's pursuer and aim for an early queen trade.

typical_structures.structure: Open position with White's f4/e4 pawns under attack and the black queen exposed on h4.

character.notes: Early queen sortie and open files give forcing, risky play for both kings.

gambit.notes: Root is a declined line; the f4 pawn is not taken, though Black may later grab e4.

soundness.notes: Generally rated dubious for Black; White gets development for the exposed queen. Unsure.

structure.notes: Open lines for pieces after early pawn exchanges.

level.notes: Rarely seen; punishing it needs known tactics.

character.reason: Early queen check and open files make play forcing and risky.

gambit.reason: Declined King's Gambit line, no pawn given up in the root.

soundness.reason: Early queen sortie is generally considered inferior.

structure.reason: Open e- and f-files and quick piece play.

level.reason: Rare tactical line, dubious so never beginner.

plans.reason: Black's queen is out early and White gains tempi.
